title: A Room for the Smile
premise: Isandro Thackeray, a meticulous pest controller who treats documentation as prayer, is hired to investigate an infestation in the village of Hollowmere—only to find handprints in the flour, teeth marks in the pews, and a church bell ringing nightly though it was melted down in 1911. The bell's song is a memory made flesh: the village's founding families fed something beneath the chapel for generations, and now it wants its verse sung by a living voice. Isandro discovers he is descended from the one family that refused to sing, and the entity has been waiting a century for his return. In the end, Isandro must choose between singing the last verse—which would bind him to Hollowmere forever beside the woman he loves—and burning the parish records, erasing the memory that keeps the thing alive, at the cost of everyone forgetting him, including her.
about_author: Juniper Nakamura is a former archivist from coastal Oregon who spent six years cataloguing defunct parish records before turning to fiction. She writes horror about paperwork, small towns, and the things that live in the gaps between entries.

chapters.title: The Contract of Small Nuisances
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He arrives in Hollowmere under a routine contract—rats in the tithe barn—and begins his ritual of photographs, measurements, and logbook entries. The village feels too quiet, too arranged. Emotional beat: the comfort of procedure masking a low, unnameable dread.

chapters.title: Fingerprints in the Flour
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He finds long, deliberate finger-drag marks through spilled flour in the millhouse, spaced like a walking gait but too wide for any animal. His documentation instinct wars with his urge to leave. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into personal fear.

chapters.title: A Bell That Was Never Cast
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At dusk the church bell rings, though the sexton shows him the 1911 receipt proving it was melted for war scrap. The villagers don't flinch; they simply go inside and lock their doors. Emotional beat: isolation—the horror of being the only one who finds it strange.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldery Keeps Her Curtains Drawn
chapters.summary: Mrs. Aldery's POV. The oldest resident remembers her grandmother humming 'the bell's song' and going out barefoot into the snow, never to return. She recognizes something in Isandro's face—his surname. Emotional beat: grief braided with guilty recognition.

chapters.title: Teeth Marks in the Pews
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Inside the chapel he documents bite gouges in the pew ends, each exactly at the height of a kneeling child. The hymnal open on the lectern is turned to a hymn whose final verse has been torn out of every copy. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Offerings
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the vestry archive he finds a century of ledgers listing payments—not money, but names, dates, and portions of grain, meat, and once, chillingly, 'one voice, paid in full.' His own family name appears as the only entry marked REFUSED, dated 1911. Emotional beat: the past reaching up and taking him by the throat.

chapters.title: What the Sexton Won't Say
chapters.summary: Sexton Bram Hale's POV. Bram tends the empty bell tower every night because his father did, and his father before him. He knows what rings the bell and why it needs a Thackeray. He lies to Isandro gently, protecting him and damning him at once. Emotional beat: duty as a slow poison.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He meets Mara Voss, the schoolteacher who came to Hollowmere two years ago and cannot remember why she stayed. Their cautious warmth over shared tea becomes the first honest conversation he's had in weeks. Emotional beat: love arriving precisely when it is most dangerous.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following scratches beneath the chapel floorboards, he finds a bricked-over crypt door warm to the touch. Through the stone, something hums the hymn—patiently, in his grandmother's voice. Emotional beat: intimacy weaponized; the thing knows how to be loved.

chapters.title: Verse One Through Four
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Isandro reconstructs the hymn from ledger marginalia: four verses bind the entity to service; the fifth, torn from every book, would free it—or free the village. The villagers begin leaving offerings on his doorstep. Emotional beat: knowledge as burden; the town has decided what he is.

chapters.title: They Leave Bread at My Door
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The offerings escalate from bread to locked boxes containing photographs of children, then a photograph of Mara asleep. The message is clear: choose, or we will choose for you. Emotional beat: the corruption of power—he holds the village's fate and they resent him for it.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Drunk in the tower, Bram admits the Hales have sung the fourth verse every solstice for a hundred years, buying time, growing hoarse and hollow. His own son left rather than inherit the duty. He begs Isandro to take up the song. Emotional beat: pity and fury entangled; duty devouring generations.

chapters.title: What Mara Forgot
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds her own arrival letter unopened in her desk, postmarked from a town she's never heard of—herself, before Hollowmere took her name from her. She realizes the entity eats memory, and that she is already half-eaten. Emotional beat: terror of self-erasure; resolve kindling.

chapters.title: The Refusal of 1911
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the county archive he finds his great-grandfather Edric Thackeray's testimony: he refused to sing the fifth verse, burned half the ledger, and fled—but the entity kept his name as collateral, waiting for blood to return. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as debt; anger at ancestors becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The village prepares the way they prepare for Christmas—lights, hush, children kept indoors—as Bram climbs the tower to sing verse four one last time. Isandro stands in the square, ledger under his arm, deciding. Emotional beat: held breath; the whole town leaning toward midnight.

chapters.title: The Bell Asks by Name
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The bell tolls his full name in place of notes. Doors open along the lane; villagers step out with candlelit faces, not menacing but pleading. The entity speaks through the chapel walls in every voice Isandro has ever loved. Emotional beat: seduction at maximum pressure—power offered as belonging.

chapters.title: Mara Sings First
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To save Isandro from choosing, Mara begins the fifth verse herself, willing to be consumed. The crypt door cracks. Isandro tackles her mid-line, and the unfinished verse hangs in the air like a wound. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal—she chooses him over the town, and it nearly dooms them both.

chapters.title: The Last Verse, Unfinished
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With the entity half-freed and the village screaming, Isandro understands the trap: finishing the verse frees it; refusing feeds it forever. There is a third option no ledger recorded—unwriting the song itself. Emotional beat: clarity in catastrophe; the moment strategy replaces fear.

chapters.title: Ash in the Baptismal Font
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He burns the remaining ledgers in the baptismal font while Bram, weeping, rings the melted bell one final time to drown the entity's counter-song. The thing beneath the chapel unravels as its memory does, shrieking in the voices of the founding dead. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; destruction as mercy.

chapters.title: The Quiet After Ringing
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Dawn. The bell is silent, the crypt cold, the village intact but strangely lighter, as if a fever broke. Bram is free; the offerings rot untouched on doorsteps. But Mara looks at Isandro with polite blankness—the price of the burning is being forgotten. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: A Room for the Smile
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He stays in Hollowmere anyway, renting a room above the mill, keeping his logbooks even though no one reads them. Each day Mara almost remembers—a smile she can't source, a name on the tip of her tongue. Emotional beat: quiet devotion; documentation transformed from prayer to courtship.

chapters.title: Entry One, Again
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sorting the school library, Mara finds Isandro's first logbook and reads her own name in it, page after page, memory returning like tide. She walks to the millhouse room and knocks. He opens the door already smiling. Emotional beat: love outlasting erasure; the record, finally, answered.
